## Findings
- claim-1: The formal conjecture is that both Theorem 5.4 generating sets for \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) are minimal. [source-6@L10-L16|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: The stronger suspected statement is \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), where \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6@L18-L21|claim=ordinary-document] [source-6@L56-L70|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-3: The authors report computational verification only for \(r\le4\) and \(q=n-r\le5\). [source-6@L46-L54|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-4: A separate open question asks for minimal generating sets for general type-\(A\) ideals \(I_w\). [source-6@L88-L102|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-5: For \(i=j=1\), \(a=\min(q-1,r-1)\), \(b=1\), and \(N=\binom{a+1}{a}=\min(r,q)\); the two displayed families specialize to \(\{h_1,\ldots,h_{\min(r,q)}\}\) and \(\{e_1,\ldots,e_{\min(r,q)}\}\).
- claim-6: If \(a=0\), equivalently \(i=q\) or \(j=r\) under \(1\le i\le q,\ 1\le j\le r\), then \(N=1\); both proposed families are the singleton \(\{s_{i^j}\}\). These are trivial minimality cases provided \(s_{i^j}\ne0\) and Theorem 5.4’s generation assertion is used.
- claim-7: The smallest interior case with \(b>1\) is \((r,q,i,j)=(3,3,2,2)\), where \(a=1\), \(b=2\), \(N=3\), and the two families are \((22,32,33)\) and \((22,221,222)\).
- claim-8: The prior finite certificate for \((r,q,i,j)=(5,6,2,2)\) gives \(N=10\), quotient \(\mathbb Z^{10}\), and basis candidates \(F_1=(22,32,33,42,43,52,44,53,54,55)\) and \(F_2=(22,221,2211,222,22111,2221,22211,2222,22221,22222)\); it supports the conjecture conditionally on the Pieri presentation and generation hypotheses. [artifact 0b05e147fd3b8f028a0683ee0de19704b04f214954cc0d8c387547f8371d7299]
- claim-9: The attempted fresh computation timed out after 10 seconds, producing no new example, counterexample, or independent verification. [artifact a52fff03e3b77fa37fcd06e5d5f57b064ca0a2f89b10901aaa4bb057bfd6006b]
- claim-10: No counterexample to minimality is supplied or obtained here.
## Strategy
Classify the supplied evidence as follows: source-backed conjecture and reported range; conditional proved support for \(i=j=1\) and proposed edge cases; artifact-backed conditional support at \((5,6,2,2)\); and unresolved candidate \((3,3,2,2)\). Use coordinatewise minimal \((r,q)\) among interior cases with \(b>1\) for “smallest.”

Record no obstructing example: the timeout produced no computation, and absence of a counterexample is not positive evidence.

## Gaps
No fresh independently verified computation was produced. In particular, \((3,3,2,2)\) has no exact quotient certificate here and remains unresolved.

The \((5,6,2,2)\) artifact is conditional support only; it lacks an independently implemented LR/Smith calculation or standalone unimodular-lattice certificate.

The general conjecture remains open; the source-reported computational range is only \(r\le4,\ q\le5\).

## Next
Supply for \((3,3,2,2)\) an exact integral LR/Smith or unimodular-lattice certificate, including all relation-row containment and basis checks for both families \((22,32,33)\) and \((22,221,222)\).

Keep all finite conclusions conditional on the box-model, Pieri/LR presentation, and Theorem 5.4 generation hypotheses until those are independently verified.
